1.1 INTRODUCTION:

1.1 To ensure an appropriate mechanism for the transfer or referral of patients who do not match the organisational resources

2.0 SCOPE:

2.1 Hospital Management

2.2 Health Care Providers

2.3 Patients

2.4 Government agencies

3.0 RESPONSIBILITY:

3.1 Doctors, Hospital Management

3.2 Nursing staff

4.0 ABBREVIATIONS:

4.1 AAC - Access Assessment and Continuity of Care

5.0 DEFINITION: Nil

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH: Accreditation Standards For Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1. Documented policies and procedures guide the transfer of patients to another facility in an appropriate manner.

7.2 Documented policies and procedures guide the transfer of stable/unstable patients to another facility appropriately.

7.3 Procedures identify staff responsible during transfer/referral.

7.4 The organisation gives a summary of the patient’s condition and the treatment given.

8. 0 PROCESSES

8.1.1 If there is no possibility of bed availability or if the patient is not agreeable to be admitted in another class (paying room), then the treating doctor is asked to possibly defer the admission of the patient or refer the patient to another centre.

8.1.2 In case of transfer of patients in a life-threatening situation (like those who are on a ventilator) to another organization, a doctor / BLS or ACLS-trained staff member accompanies the patient. The ambulance driver, attendant, male nurse (Trained in BLS and/or ACLS), or doctor accompanies during transfer for unstable Patients to other organisations.

8.2 TRANSFER OF STABLE PATIENTS

Stable Patient is transferred to another organization through the ambulance, accompanied by the ambulance driver, attendant and nurse (Trained in BLS). To provide a mechanism to facilitate the “appropriate transfer” of stable, nonemergent patients who request such a transfer.

8.2.1 DEFINITIONS An “appropriate transfer” is defined as one in which: The receiving facility has available resources and agrees to accept the transfer and provide necessary treatment, and the transferring facility provides the receiving hospital with a complete copy of the patient’s records and other information (such as discharge summary, copies of X-rays, etc.), and the transfer is effected through qualified personnel and transportation equipment, including use of necessary and medically appropriate life support measures during the transfer.

8.2.2 It is the policy of the Hospital to accept the transfer of stable, non-emergent patients when space, facilities, and personnel are available. Every effort shall be made to accept patients when the sending facility does not have the space, facilities or personnel to provide safe and appropriate care.

a)Transfers of stable, non-emergent patients to a higher referral centre may be made by contacting a consultant physician of the Hospital.

b)Stable, non-emergent transfers shall be directly admitted to hospital units.

c) Acceptance of stable, non-emergent patients for transfer to the Hospital shall be made contingent upon verification of available resources.

d)Transportation arrangements for patients to be transferred from the Hospital shall be made through the Residential Medical Officer.

e) Similarly, when resources matching the patient needs are not available at Hospital, patients shall be transferred to facilities that can meet the patient’s needs. Appropriate transportation arrangements and a medical escort (if needed) shall be made through the Residential Medical Officer.

8.2.3 TRANSFER OF UNSTABLE PATIENTS

Medically Unstable Patient is transferred to another organization through the ambulance, accompanied by ambulance driver, attendant and nurse (Trained in BLS).

DEFINITIONS

Medically unstable condition- The term “medically unstable condition” means – A medical condition manifesting itself by acute symptoms of sufficient severity (including severe pain) such that the absence of immediate medical attention could reasonably be expected to result in – Placing the health of the individual (or, with respect to a pregnant woman, the health of the woman or her unborn child) in serious jeopardy, Serious impairment of bodily functions .Serious dysfunction of any bodily organ or part Stabilised - The term “stabilized” means with respect to a medically unstable condition, for which no material deterioration of the condition is likely, within reasonable medical probability, to result from or occur during the transfer of the individual from a facility.

8.2.3.1 Requests from other health care providers to transfer patients who have an emergency medical condition and require emergency and tertiary level medical care not available at that facility should be immediately approved when services, space, facilities, and personnel are available to provide appropriate care.

• When Patients admitted to the hospital are unstable may be transferred to other hospitals only when adequate facilities and qualified personnel are available to provide appropriate and continuous care during transfer..

• When the facility making the transfer request is capable of providing the necessary care, that facility must stabilise the emergency medical condition before transfer.

• When the transferring facility is requesting the transfer of an unstable patient, the following conditions must be met

• Physician certification that the expected benefits of transfer outweigh the risks of transfer

• Patient or family consent when possible

• Attempts made by the transferring hospital, within its capability, to stabilize the patient to minimise any risks to the individual during transfer

• Our capacity and capability to treat the transferred patient

• Delivery of all appropriate medical records

• Transfer shall be made with qualified personnel and transportation equipment.

• If an emergency patient requires services not available at Hospital, the transfer shall be refused with a recommendation to contact another facility with the necessary capability.

• Transfer of patients shall be made by the referring physician contacting Consultant / Senior Consultant /Residential officer.

• All departments who receive requests for transfer of patients shall maintain this policy and procedure statement in a place accessible to medical staff, and other personnel to ensure that physicians who are involved in transfers adhere to its content. Questions shall be referred to Chief Medical Superintendent.

• Similarly, when resources matching the patient needs are not available at Hospital patients shall be transferred to Shalinitai Meghe Hospital and Research Centre, Nagpur that can meet the patient’s needs. The Consultant / Residents shall contact the faculty of the receiving hospital to ensure that eligibility guidelines are met. Transportation arrangements

and a medical escort (if needed) shall be made through the Residential Medical Officer.

Indications for transfer to another facility:

• Non-availability of beds at all.

• Patient desires to be transferred to another facility

• Services are not available at the hospital

• Patients being transferred from the Hospital shall be accompanied by a transfer summary that shall include details of the patient medical condition, interventions done and the ongoing needs of the patient. Such transfers shall be accompanied by the residential medical officer. Stabilization prior to transfer shall include securing the airway (if needed), intravenous access, appropriate fluid replacement and pain control.

8.3 The trained BLS staff is arranged by the Resident Medical Officer. Information is given to their respective HODs. If ALS ambulance is required, then arrangement is made from SMHRC, with a doctor in coordination with CMS SMHRC.

8.4 The organization provide a case summary mentioning the significant findings and treatment given in the case of patients who are being transferred from the emergency. A copy of the same shall be retained by the organisation. For admitted patients, a discharge summary has to be given (refer AAC 13 & 14). The same shall also be given to patients leaving against medical advice. This shall include patients being transferred both for diagnostic and/or therapeutic purposes.
